extracted.intended_audience: researchers and peer reviewers (including junior researchers) interested in post-publication peer review and research integrity
extracted.subtask_description: Overview and evaluation of PubPeer 2.0 as a platform for post-publication peer review, describing features, benefits, and potential drawbacks for scientists and reviewers. Aimed at people considering using or understanding post-publication commenting systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strong anonymity guarantees
rubrics_metrics.description: PubPeer 2.0 provides enhanced and more secure anonymity; users can choose anonymity that is 'now more secure and guaranteed' and obtain accounts with a pseudonym assigned via a 'tree of life' code that is safeguarded by the user.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article highlights that enhanced anonymity makes it 'near impossible for anyone to know your real identity.' This is presented as a strength because it encourages participation (especially junior researchers) and can mitigate conflicts of interest, but also raises debate about openness and accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account types and identity options (signed vs pseudonymous)
rubrics_metrics.description: A signed account is still available and is not anonymous to readers who can access the website’s contents, while pseudonymous/anonymous accounts remain an option.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The platform preserves both identifiable (signed) and anonymous/pseudonymous participation, implying a trade-off between transparency (signed) and protection for reviewers (pseudonymous). Choice of account type affects how comments are perceived and the degree of accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account authenticity and vetting for grey-listed/pseudonymous accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: The authenticity of your grey listed account requires vetting before approval; users can obtain an account with just a code (safeguarded by the user).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vetting is used to provide some assurance of authenticity while preserving anonymity. This reduces the risk of sock-puppetry or malicious accounts and is intended to balance anonymity with credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moderation for factual accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: All the comments go through moderation (for facts and truth).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moderation is emphasized as a quality-control mechanism so that posted comments are checked for factual correctness. The article ties moderation to professionalization of comments and to the platform's role in driving corrections and retractions when warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional and academic tone of comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments related to methods, images or more will be more professional and academic under PubPeer 2.0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The post suggests that improved moderation, formatting, and features will foster more scholarly-quality comments, attracting domain experts (e.g., mathematicians and physicists) and elevating the level of discourse beyond social-media style remarks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for technical formatting (LaTeX support)
rubrics_metrics.description: PubPeer 2.0 platform now supports LaTeX equations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LaTeX support is singled out as a feature likely to increase participation from mathematically and technically intensive fields, enabling precise technical critique (equations, formulae) within comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Previewing comments for spelling and grammar
rubrics_metrics.description: A new feature is the pre-viewing of comments (to detect any spelling and grammatical error).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Previewing aims to improve the polish and readability of comments visible to readers, raising perceived professionalism and reducing superficial distractions from substantive critique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improved reading/formatting and chronological presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments will be more professionally formatted and will appear in chronological order to the readers with embedded links.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Better formatting, embedded links, and chronological ordering enhance usability and make it easier for readers to follow a conversation and verify sources referenced in comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centralization and searchability of post-publication review
rubrics_metrics.description: PubPeer 2.0 centralizes the post-publication peer review process, making it easy to search from anywhere by anyone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Centralization improves discoverability of critiques and discussions across journals and disciplines. The article suggests this accessibility can motivate researchers to improve study design and reporting prior to publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Efficacy in correcting the published record
rubrics_metrics.description: Factual and verifiable feedback on PubPeer has led to many editorial corrections, and even retractions because of discovered research misconduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The platform's ability to surface verifiable problems (e.g., image issues, methodological flaws) is presented as a real-world outcome demonstrating its value for research integrity and post-publication quality control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk of social-media-like dynamics degrading objectivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Allowing post-publication peer review to develop along a Facebook or Twitter model may make it difficult to share objective reviews on flaws and merits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article cautions that if post-publication platforms prioritize engagement or adopt social-media norms, discourse may become less objective or equitable, potentially harming fair evaluation of research and disadvantaging qualified reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouraging junior researchers' participation and mitigating conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Enhanced anonymity helps junior researchers participate in peer review without reservations when reviewing the work of their peers or experienced researchers; when coupled to an open post-publication peer review process, it can also mitigate potential conflicts of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anonymity plus open public discussion lowers barriers for junior scientists to voice concerns and can serve as an alternative check when journal-assigned peer review may be conflicted. However, the trade-offs between openness and protection must be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential resistance from for-profit subscription journals
rubrics_metrics.description: For-profit subscription journals generally remain uninterested in the post-publication peer review process, as it may cast doubt on the quality of their journal content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adoption barriers exist: publishers may view third-party post-publication critique as undermining their brand/quality control. This affects the platform's integration with formal publishing workflows and its influence across journals.
